simple.meaning: אׇכְלָה (ʼoklâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “food.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 18 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Genesis 1:29. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אׇכְלָה (H402).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H402. oklah אָכְלָה 17 noun feminine food, eating (with some verbal force, compare Dr JPh xi. 217 ) only P, & Ezekiel; always לְאָכְלָה , 1 especially in phrase like לְאָ יִהְיֶה ׳לָכֶם Gen 1:29 ; 6:21 ; 9:3 ; Lev 11:39 ; so 25:6 לְאָבְלָה לָכֶם הָאָרֶץ שַׁבַּת וְהָיְתָה compare לְא ׳נָתַן Gen 1:30 ; Exod 16:15 . 2 devouring , by wild beasts, only figurative of ravaged people Ezek 29:5 ; 34:5 , 8 , 10 ; 39:4 , compare 35:12 . 3 consumimg , in fire Ezek 15:4 , 6 , of fire-sacrifice of children 23:37 ; figurative of judgment of ׳י Ezekiel 21:37; (compare also infinitive of אָכַל ).

occurrences.englishText: God said, “Behold,† “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.
To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it was so.
Take with you some of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it will be for food for you, and for them.”
Every moving thing that lives will be food for you. As I gave you the green herb, I have given everything to you.
When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread which Yahweh has given you to eat.
“ ‘If any animal of which you may eat dies, he who touches its carcass shall be unclean until the evening.
The Sabbath of the land shall be for food for you; for yourself, for your servant, for your maid, for your hired servant, and for your stranger, who lives as a foreigner with you.
Is my heritage to me as a speckled bird of prey?
Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire has devoured both its ends, and the middle of it is burned. Is it profitable for any work?
Therefore the Lord Yahweh says: “As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I will give the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

For they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols. They have also caused their sons, whom they bore to me, to pass through the fire to them to be devoured.
I’ll cast you out into the wilderness,
They were scattered, because there was no shepherd. They became food to all the animals of the field, and were scattered.

“As I live,” says the Lord Yahweh, “surely because my sheep became a prey, and my sheep became food to all the animals of the field, because there was no shepherd. My shepherds didn’t search for my sheep, but the shepherds fed themselves, and didn’t feed my sheep.”

The Lord Yahweh says: “Behold, I am against the shepherds. I will require my sheep at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the sheep. The shepherds won’t feed themselves any more. I will deliver my sheep from their mouth, that they may not be food for them.”
You will know that I, Yahweh, have heard all your insults which you have spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, ‘They have been laid desolate. They have been given us to devour.’

You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you, and all your hordes, and the peoples who are with you. I will give you to the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the animals of the field to be devoured.
